sections.body: Third-and-long decides the game. New England drops back on 92.7% of those snaps [mc1], but 41 plays [mc2] is a small sample. LAC's offense is at -0.13 EPA per play [mc3], so it cannot afford stalls; the defense needs pressure and tight coverage on those downs. New England allows conversions on 39.8% of third downs [mc4] over 123 plays [mc5], ranked 17th [mc6], so LAC should use quick, high-percentage throws. New England sends five or more rushers on 35.2% of dropbacks [mc7] over 355 plays [mc8], so protection and hot throws decide whether the blitz becomes a stall. With Henderson out, Stevenson's 46.0% share of team rushes [mc10] becomes the run plan, so load the A-gaps. New England allows 0.12 EPA per pass play [mc14] and 10.1% explosive passes [mc15], so keep the deep ball off the table. Test the new looks with McConkey, questionable at 11.8% [mc16]; if he sits, Kolar, also questionable, takes 8.9% of targets [mc17].
